items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee (Maxine Sullivan) does not mention Eleanor Campbell; the mention is made by the Interviewer regarding their own father's wife.

ctx.x: My dad, Chester Campbell, Sr., was born in Cumberland, Maryland. He was an orphan and the man that raised him taught him to play the E-flat tuba.

He went on the road with a show called, In Old Kentucky when he was a youngster and in 1926 he brought his bride, Eleanor Campbell and his four youngsters to New York. He played with Cliff Jackson, he played a stint with Earl Hines, he played a stint with Cab Calloway. He switched to the string bass around the early 30s and he took lessons from a German fella for $2.00 a lesson in the front room of our home.
Where was your home at that time?
